doc.title: Meta App Review: permissions, test calls, screencast and words to paste
doc.text:
# ChurchConnect's Meta App Review: what to ask for, and the words to paste

What we are asking Meta for: a church writes a post once in ChurchConnect and it publishes to the church's own Facebook Page and linked Instagram Business account. Nothing else.

This needs a computer. All of it happens at developers.facebook.com in the app named **Church Connect**.

## Ask for exactly these six permissions

| Permission | Why the app needs it | Test call (Graph API Explorer, app = Church Connect) |
|---|---|---|
| `pages_show_list` | List the Pages the admin chose so we can save them as channels | `GET /me/accounts` |
| `pages_read_engagement` | Read the Page's name and its linked Instagram account | `GET /{page-id}?fields=name,instagram_business_account` |
| `pages_manage_posts` | Publish the church's post to its Page | `POST /{page-id}/feed` with `message=Test from ChurchConnect` (then delete it) |
| `instagram_basic` | Read the linked Instagram Business account's id and username | `GET /{ig-user-id}?fields=id,username` |
| `instagram_content_publish` | Publish the church's photo or video to Instagram | `POST /{ig-user-id}/media` with `image_url=…&caption=Test`, then `POST /{ig-user-id}/media_publish` with `creation_id=…` |
| `business_management` | Pages owned through a Business Portfolio only appear with it | `GET /me/businesses` |

Use a **Page** token (from `/me/accounts`) for the Page and Instagram calls. Test calls take up to 24 hours to show as "1 of 1".

## Steps in the Meta dashboard

1. **App Review → Permissions and Features:** remove every requested item that is not in the table above (ads, WhatsApp, Threads, Messenger, fundraisers, catalog, branded content, leads, `instagram_manage_comments`, `instagram_manage_messages`, `pages_manage_engagement`, and so on). Add `instagram_content_publish`; it was never requested.
2. **Facebook Login for Business → Settings → Valid OAuth Redirect URIs:** add `https://www.churchconnect.cloud/api/social/meta/callback`
3. **Facebook Login for Business → Configurations:** there should already be one of type "User access token" with the six permissions above and assets Pages + Instagram accounts. If there is not, create it and tell an agent.
4. Nothing to copy. The App ID, App Secret and Configuration ID are already saved on ChurchConnect (checked 2026-11-10).
5. **App roles → Testers:** until Meta approves, only people with a role on the app can finish the Facebook sign-in. Record the screencast as one of them.
6. The church's Instagram must be a Business account linked to the Page.

## The screencast (one recording, about 90 seconds, reused for every permission)

Record at `https://www.churchconnect.cloud`, in English, with the cursor visible and no cuts during the sign-in. Turn on captions, or add a text label naming each permission as it is used.

1. Signed in as a church admin, open **Social Media → Channels**.
2. Click **Connect Facebook & Instagram**.
3. In the Facebook window: show the account, select the church **Page** and its **Instagram account**, show the permission list, click **Continue/Save**. (pages_show_list, business_management)
4. Back in ChurchConnect: a green banner says "Connected 1 Facebook Page and 1 Instagram account". Open Facebook and Instagram: the Page name and @username show. (pages_read_engagement, instagram_basic)
5. **Overview → New Post**: type an event announcement, attach a flyer image, tick the Facebook and Instagram channels, click **Publish**.
6. The scheduler shows both posts **Published**. (pages_manage_posts, instagram_content_publish)
7. Open the church's Facebook Page in a new tab: the post is there. Open the Instagram profile: the post is there.
8. Back in Channels, click the trash icon on a channel: it disconnects.

## Descriptions to paste

**pages_show_list** — ChurchConnect is software churches use to run announcements and events. A church admin clicks "Connect Facebook & Instagram" and chooses their church's Page in the Facebook Login dialog. We call `GET /me/accounts` once to list the Pages they chose, and save each as a publishing channel for that church. Without it we cannot know which Page the church wants to post to. The screencast shows the dialog and the Page appearing in Channels.

**pages_read_engagement** — After the admin connects, we read the Page's name and its linked Instagram Business account (`GET /{page-id}?fields=name,instagram_business_account`) so the admin can see which Page and Instagram account are connected and pick them when posting. We do not read posts, comments, or follower data.

**pages_manage_posts** — The core feature: a church writes an event or announcement once in ChurchConnect and clicks Publish; we post it to the church's own Page with `POST /{page-id}/feed` (or `/photos` with the flyer). We only post content the admin wrote and explicitly published. The screencast shows a post published from ChurchConnect appearing on the Page.

**instagram_basic** — We read the connected Instagram Business account's id and username so the admin can see which account is connected and select it when publishing. No other Instagram data is read.

**instagram_content_publish** — The same post the admin publishes to Facebook is published to the church's Instagram with its flyer image or video, using `POST /{ig-user-id}/media` and `/media_publish`. Only content the admin wrote and chose to publish is posted. The screencast shows it appearing on the Instagram profile.

**business_management** — Many churches' Pages are owned by a Business Portfolio; without this permission those Pages are missing from the Facebook Login result and the church cannot connect. We use it only to list the Pages and Instagram accounts the admin granted in the dialog.

**Add this to the end of each one:** Data is used only to show the church admin which accounts are connected and to publish what they choose to publish. It is never sold, shared, or used for advertising. Page tokens are stored server-side, never shown in the browser, and deleted when the admin disconnects or removes the app from Facebook (data deletion callback: `https://www.churchconnect.cloud/api/webhooks/meta/data-deletion`).

doc.title: The eight governments and the note each would get
doc.text:
# Commons outreach: the soft sale

Your idea (2026-11-04): don't tell a government its site has problems. Hand them a free report so they see it themselves, the way a resident does.

## The report is the pitch

- **What's working comes first.** Toombs posts its agendas on time; the report says so before anything else.
- **No grade.** It reads "4 things working well, 5 a resident would notice."
- **Every issue has a fix anyone can do by hand.** Commons is offered last, for when keeping up is the hard part.
- It is a link a clerk can forward to the commission without it reading like a sales sheet.

## The first eight: Toombs and its neighbors

Results from the first scan (2026-11-04). An agent runs it again on the day the notes go out, so the numbers and links are fresh.

| Government | Result |
|---|---|
| Toombs County | 4 working, 5 to notice (a 7.5-year-old calendar, empty Bids and Jobs pages) |
| City of Vidalia | 3 working, 2 to notice |
| City of Lyons | 3 working, 5 to notice |
| Tattnall County | 3 working, 4 to notice |
| Emanuel County | 5 working, 1 to notice. In good shape; low priority |
| Jeff Davis County | 2 working, 5 to notice |
| Appling County | 2 working, 5 to notice |
| Montgomery County | Its site turns away automated readers. Skipped; we don't work around that |

## The note each one gets

Every government gets the same short note, with its own name, its own report link and its own opening line. This is the wording:

**Subject:** A free report on Toombs County's website

Hello,

I noticed your agendas page is up to date — more than a lot of counties manage. I ran a free checkup that reads the site the way a resident would — the calendar, agendas, notices, bids, and jobs pages — and lists what's working and what a resident might notice, with a simple fix for each.

Here it is, no sign-up needed: (the link to that government's own report)

Everything in it can be fixed by hand. If keeping the site current is the hard part, we also make a tool that does that, but the report is yours either way.

(Your name)
(Phone) · (Organization)

Where a site has nothing current to praise, the opening line is instead: "I was looking at the City of Lyons' website and put together a short report on it."

## The rules

1. **Nothing is sent automatically.** A person sends each note by hand, under their own name.
2. Each note goes to the address the government itself publishes for its clerk or manager. No guessed addresses.
3. One note per government. No follow-ups. If they open the report and don't reply, that is an answer.
4. Start with the three most out-of-date sites: Toombs, Jeff Davis and Appling. Send more only if those get replies.

## How we know if it worked

The Commons admin page shows each report, how many times it was opened, and whether a government signed up from it.

doc.text:
# Online giving: connecting Tithe.ly, or replacing it with Stripe

You asked (2026-11-09), after seeing that Mocks Church gives through Tithe.ly: "Look into actually connecting with Tithely and look at the ways we could replace Tithely if the church wants to, like with the integration through Stripe."

Everything below was checked on 2026-11-09 in the ChurchConnect code, its database, or on Tithe.ly's and Stripe's own pages.

## The short version

- Tithe.ly does not give outside software a way to read a church's gifts. So gifts cannot flow from Tithe.ly into ChurchConnect on their own. Only Tithe.ly can change that.
- What works today: the church downloads its gifts from Tithe.ly as a spreadsheet and uploads it to ChurchConnect.
- The only way gifts arrive with no upload is for ChurchConnect to take the gifts itself, through Stripe. That is a bigger build, and it involves money and Stripe's terms.

## What ChurchConnect does today

- **It takes no gifts itself.** The member "Give" button sends the giver to the church's own giving page.
- **It records gifts by hand or by spreadsheet.** Finances → Record giving, and Import giving. Those gifts feed Reports, the budget and year-end statements.
- **There is old Tithe.ly code that does not work.** It saves an account name and key but never brings in a gift. No church has ever used it (0 rows in the database).

## Connecting Tithe.ly

What Tithe.ly publishes ([tithe.ly/api](https://tithe.ly/api)):

- Access is "available by request" for a church that uses Tithe.ly. Requests go to support@tithe.ly.
- The published connection can **create** a gift. There is **no published way to list a church's gifts**, and no automatic notice when a gift comes in.

So an automatic "Tithe.ly gifts flow into ChurchConnect" connection cannot be built from what Tithe.ly publishes. Only Tithe.ly can say whether a partner gets more.

What does work for a church on Tithe.ly:

- **Export, then import.** Tithe.ly's dashboard exports gifts to a spreadsheet. ChurchConnect's Import giving takes that file today.
- Worth building (small): remember each church's column match, skip a gift that was already imported, and match Tithe.ly's categories to the church's funds. Then a weekly or monthly import is one step.

Tithe.ly's fees, from its pricing page: card 2.9% + 30 cents, bank transfer 1% + 30 cents, no monthly fee for giving.

## Replacing Tithe.ly with Stripe

Two levels:

1. **No build.** The church makes its own Stripe payment link and uses it as its giving page. This already works. Gifts still have to be imported, the same as Tithe.ly.
2. **ChurchConnect giving through Stripe.** Each church opens its own Stripe account from inside ChurchConnect. Gifts go straight to the church's bank. Stripe tells ChurchConnect about each gift, so it lands in Finances, Reports, the budget and the year-end statement with no import.

What level 2 needs built: church sign-up with Stripe, a giving page per church (funds, one-time and repeating, card and bank), refunds and receipts.

- Stripe offers eligible nonprofits 2.2% + 30 cents on donations. Whether that rate carries through when the gift comes through ChurchConnect is **not confirmed**; Stripe has to be asked.
- Either Stripe bills each church directly and ChurchConnect takes nothing, or ChurchConnect adds its own small fee on each gift. That is your call.
- Only you can: turn on Connect in the right Stripe account, accept Stripe's platform terms, and decide whether ChurchConnect takes a fee.

## What the agent recommends

1. Now: tell churches on Tithe.ly to keep it, and bring their giving in by export and import. True today, nothing to build.
2. Next (small build): make importing a Tithe.ly export one step.
3. Email Tithe.ly (support@tithe.ly) to ask whether a partner can list a church's gifts.
4. Decide later, when a church actually asks to leave Tithe.ly, whether to build giving through Stripe.
5. Remove the old Tithe.ly code that does not work, so no one mistakes it for a working connection. (An agent does this; no decision needed.)

# Operate and Snip.show: what is built, and the one open question

You asked (2026-11-09) for Operate to "manage marketing campaigns that revolve around videos that are put on TikTok and YouTube and Facebook", and for it to connect with Snip.show so businesses can manage their content.

## What is built in Operate (waiting to go live)

- A shop makes a **campaign**: which places to post (TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn), the start date, how many weeks and how many posts a week.
- Operate lays out a dated calendar. Each post has its caption, cut to that platform's length, a copy button, and a link straight to the upload page.
- **Operate does not post for the shop.** A person posts, then pastes the link back. A post only counts as posted once it has that link.
- **Operate does not hold the videos.** A clip is a title and a link to something that lives in Snip.show or on the shop's phone.

## Why there is a question for you

Snip.show today is built for **one creator: you**. Every video and every clip belongs to a single sign-in. There is no "business" anywhere in it.

So an Operate shop can plan and record its posts today, and link out to Snip.show, but it **cannot keep its own clips in Snip.show**.

The ecosystem rule is "do not run a second clipper", so Operate must not grow its own clip library instead. Which way this goes changes what Snip.show is, so it is your call.

## The choices

- **(a) Snip.show gains businesses.** An Operate shop signs in to Snip.show and keeps its own clips there. This is a real build in Snip.show (every video and clip needs to know which business owns it), and it changes Snip.show from "your tool" to "a tool shops use".
- **(b) Snip.show stays yours alone.** Shops cut their clips however they like (their phone, CapCut, anything) and paste the links into Operate. Nothing more to build. This is how it works the moment the campaigns page goes live.
- **(c) Something else you have in mind.**

If you pick (a), one more question: Snip.show already records a 20 percent share on clip earnings for creators. Would that share apply to a business's clips, or only to creators?

# Your first marketing client: the message to send

Your tennis student already asked you for a website and help getting the word out. That makes them the warmest lead you have: they know you, and they asked. Nobody else on any of our lists has done that.

## The message (copy, change any words you like, and text it)

Hey, I've been thinking about what you asked me, the website and getting the word out.

Here's what I can do. I build your page, then plan and post for you every week (pictures and short videos), and each month I send you a plain report of what came in.

One post a week is $150 a month. Three a week is $350. The page is a one-time $150. You'd be my first client for this, so the first month is half price if you'll let me show the results to others. You can stop at the end of any month.

Want to sit down this week so I can show you a plan?

## If they say yes, ask for these (a text back is fine)

1. The name of the business and what they sell or do
2. Who they want to reach (the town, the kind of customer)
3. Their Facebook or Instagram page, if they have one
4. Five to ten photos from their phone
5. The phone number or email customers should use
6. Anything coming up: an event, a sale, a new season

## Then tell me

Say "the tennis student said yes" in chat and paste what they sent. I build the page and the first month's plan the same day, and you approve the posts before anything goes out.

## What it is, in one line

The Word Out Pack: https://www.we-succeed.org/word-out
